nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program, let $R$ be the sum over the instructions of $p$ of the largest register index each one mentions, and let $s'$ be a state that $p$ reaches from the state $s$ in one step. Then the coded step, run on the list of codes of the instructions of $p$, sends the coded state of $s$ (its program counter together with the list of the contents of its registers $0, \dots, R$) to the coded state of $s'$.
nodes.title: A machine step is a coded step

nodes.summary: A coded state is a program counter $k$ together with a list $r$ of register contents (in use, the contents of registers $0, \dots, R$, where $R$ is the register bound of the program), and a program is given by the list $c$ of its instruction codes. Write $c_k$ for entry $k$ of $c$, and $r_j$ for entry $j$ of $r$, read as $0$ when $j$ is past the end of $r$; setting an entry past the end of $r$ leaves $r$ unchanged.…
nodes.title: One coded URM step

nodes.summary: For every URM program $p$, the function sending an input $x$ and a step count $t$ to the output of $p$ on $x$ after $t$ steps (nothing while $p$ is still running, the contents of register $0$ once it has halted) is a computable function of the pair $(x, t)$.
nodes.title: The URM output after a given number of steps is computable

nodes.summary: If a predicate $P$ on the natural numbers is URM-decidable, then it is a computable predicate: its Boolean decision function, sending $n$ to whether $P(n)$ holds, is computable.
nodes.title: A URM-decidable predicate is computable

nodes.summary: A predicate $P$ on the natural numbers is URM-decidable when some URM program computes its characteristic function: started on any input $n$ (register $0$ holding $n$, all other registers $0$), the program halts, and register $0$ then holds $1$ if $P(n)$ holds and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: URM-decidable predicate

nodes.summary: For every URM instruction $I$, unpairing the code of $I$ gives first component $0$ if $I$ is a zero instruction $Z\,n$, $1$ if it is a successor instruction $S\,n$, $2$ if it is a transfer $T\,m\,n$, and $3$ if it is a jump $J\,m\,n\,q$.
nodes.title: Tag of an instruction code

nodes.summary: Write $\langle a, b \rangle$ for the pairing of natural numbers $a$ and $b$. For every URM instruction $I$, unpairing the code of $I$ gives second component $n$ if $I$ is $Z\,n$ or $S\,n$, $\langle m, n \rangle$ if $I$ is $T\,m\,n$, and $\langle m, \langle n, q \rangle \rangle$ if $I$ is $J\,m\,n\,q$.
nodes.title: Payload of an instruction code

nodes.summary: Code of a URM instruction as a natural number: the instruction tag paired with the paired arguments, `Z n ↦ pair 0 n`, `S n ↦ pair 1 n`, `T m n ↦ pair 2 (pair m n)`, `J m n q ↦ pair 3 (pair m (pair n q))`.
nodes.title: Code of a URM instruction

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a list of instruction codes, $s$ a coded state, and $t_1 \le t_2$ natural numbers. If after $t_1$ steps of bounded execution of $c$ from $s$ the program counter is at least the length of $c$, then $t_2$ steps of bounded execution of $c$ from $s$ give the same coded state as $t_1$ steps.
nodes.title: Bounded URM execution stays at its halted value

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a list of instruction codes, $s$ a coded state and $t$ a natural number. If after $t$ steps of bounded execution of $c$ from $s$ the program counter is at least the length of $c$, then $t + 1$ steps of bounded execution of $c$ from $s$ give the same coded state as $t$ steps.
nodes.title: Bounded URM execution is stable once halted

nodes.summary: For a list of instruction codes, a number $t$ and a coded state $s$, bounded execution for $t + 1$ steps from $s$ is the one-step function applied to the result of bounded execution for $t$ steps from $s$.
nodes.title: Bounded execution unfolds by one step

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program, $x$ an input and $t$ a natural number. Then there is a machine state $s'$, reachable from the initial state with input list $[x]$ by steps of $p$, whose coded state equals the result of bounded execution for $t$ steps on the instruction codes of $p$ from the initial coded state for $x$.
nodes.title: Bounded execution only reaches codes of reachable states

nodes.summary: For a list of instruction codes, a number $t$ and a coded state $s$, bounded execution applies the one-step function for these codes $t$ times, starting from $s$.
nodes.title: Bounded execution

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program and $x$ an input. If a machine state $s$ is reachable from the initial state with input list $[x]$ by steps of $p$, then for some number $t$, bounded execution for $t$ steps on the instruction codes of $p$ from the initial coded state for $x$ gives the coded state of $s$.
nodes.title: Every reachable state is reached by bounded execution

nodes.summary: If the URM program $p$ has instruction $I$ at position $pc$, then the entry at position $pc$ of the list of instruction codes of $p$, read with default $0$, is the code of $I$.
nodes.title: Instruction codes by position

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program with register bound $R$ and $\sigma$ a register state. For every $n$, the entry at position $n$ of the register list of $\sigma$, read with default $0$, is $\sigma(n)$ if $n \le R$ and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Reading the register list

nodes.summary: For a URM program $p$, an input $x$ and a number $t$, run bounded execution for $t$ steps on the instruction codes of $p$ from the initial coded state for $x$. If the resulting program counter is less than the length of the list of instruction codes, the program is still running and there is no output; otherwise the output is the entry at position $0$ of the resulting register list, read with default $0$.
nodes.title: Output after a given number of steps

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program, $x$ an input and $t$ a number. If bounded execution for $t$ steps on the instruction codes of $p$ from the initial coded state for $x$ reaches a program counter at least the length of the list of instruction codes, then $p$ halts on the input list $[x]$.
nodes.title: A halted coded state gives a halting machine run

nodes.summary: For a URM program $p$ and an input $x$, the initial coded state for $x$ equals the coded state of the initial machine state with input list $[x]$.
nodes.title: The initial coded state codes the initial machine state

nodes.summary: For a URM program $p$ with register bound $R$ and an input $x$, the initial coded state has program counter $0$ and register list $(x, 0, \dots, 0)$ of length $R + 1$: register $0$ holds $x$ and registers $1, \dots, R$ hold $0$.
nodes.title: Initial coded state

nodes.summary: For a URM program $p$ with register bound $R$ and a register state $\sigma$, the register list of $\sigma$ (the contents of registers $0, \dots, R$) has length $R + 1$.
nodes.title: Length of the register list

nodes.summary: For a URM program $p$ with register bound $R$ and every instruction $I$ of $p$, the largest register index referenced by $I$ is at most $R$.
nodes.title: Instructions stay within the register bound

nodes.summary: A coded state is a pair $(c, \ell)$ of a natural number $c$ and a list $\ell$ of natural numbers. Its machine state has program counter $c$, and register $n$ holds the $n$-th entry of $\ell$ (counting from $0$) when $n$ is less than the length of $\ell$, and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Decoding a coded state

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a partial function from $\mathbb{N}$ to $\mathbb{N}$. Suppose some URM program has the following property for every natural number $x$: started with $x$ in register $0$ and all other registers $0$, it halts exactly when $f(x)$ is defined, and then it holds $f(x)$ in register $0$. Then $f$ is partial recursive.
nodes.title: A URM-computable partial function is partial recursive

nodes.summary: If a state $s$ of a URM program $p$ makes a step to some state, then the program counter of $s$ is less than the number of instructions of $p$.
nodes.title: A state that can step is running

nodes.summary: The coded step is primitive recursive, for any fixed list of instruction codes.
nodes.title: The coded step is primitive recursive

nodes.summary: For a URM program $p$, the bounded execution of $p$ for $t$ steps ($t$ iterations of the one-step function on the list of instruction codes of $p$), started from the initial coded state for input $x$, is a primitive recursive function of the pair $(x, t)$.
nodes.title: Bounded execution is primitive recursive in the input and the step bound

nodes.summary: The initial coded state is primitive recursive in the input.
nodes.title: The initial coded state is primitive recursive in the input

nodes.summary: For every list of natural numbers, read as instruction codes, the function on coded states (pairs of a program counter and a register list) that sends a coded state to its successor under one coded step, and a coded state with no successor to itself, is primitive recursive.
nodes.title: The one-step function is primitive recursive

nodes.summary: A URM-recognizable predicate is recursively enumerable.
nodes.title: A URM-recognizable predicate is recursively enumerable

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program. If $n$ is a register read by some instruction of $p$, then $n$ is at most the register bound of $p$.
nodes.title: Registers read by a program lie within the register bound

nodes.summary: A predicate $P$ on the natural numbers is URM-recognizable when there is a URM program that, started with input $n$ in register $0$ and every other register $0$, halts if and only if $P(n)$ holds.
nodes.title: URM-recognizable predicates

nodes.summary: The register bound $R$ of a URM program $p$ is the sum, over the instructions of $p$, of the largest register index each instruction refers to. Every register that an instruction of $p$ can read or write is at most $R$.
nodes.title: Register bound

nodes.summary: A URM-decidable predicate is decidable by a single-tape Turing machine.
nodes.title: A URM-decidable predicate is decidable by a single-tape Turing machine

nodes.summary: A URM-recognizable predicate is recognizable by a single-tape Turing machine.
nodes.title: A URM-recognizable predicate is recognizable by a single-tape Turing machine

nodes.summary: Given a list of instruction codes, the one-step function sends a coded state $s$ to the result of one coded URM step from $s$ when that step is defined, and leaves $s$ unchanged when it is not (in particular when $s$ is halted).
nodes.title: One-step function on coded states

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program and $s$ a machine state. If one coded URM step, run on the list of codes of the instructions of $p$ from the coded state of $s$, yields $c'$, then there is a machine state $s'$ such that $p$ steps from $s$ to $s'$ in one step and the coded state of $s'$ is $c'$.
nodes.title: A coded step is a machine step

nodes.summary: A URM-decidable predicate is decidable by a multi-stack Turing machine.
nodes.title: A URM-decidable predicate is decidable by a multi-stack Turing machine

nodes.summary: A URM-recognizable predicate is recognizable by a multi-stack Turing machine.
nodes.title: A URM-recognizable predicate is recognizable by a multi-stack Turing machine

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program with register bound $R$, and let $c$ be a coded state: a program counter together with a list of register contents. If the list has length $R + 1$, then the coded state, with respect to $p$, of the machine state decoded from $c$ is $c$.
nodes.title: Decoding and re-encoding a coded state gives it back

nodes.summary: For a URM program $p$ with register bound $R$, the coded state of a machine state $s$ is the pair consisting of the program counter of $s$ and the register list $(r_0, \dots, r_R)$ of the contents of registers $0, \dots, R$ of $s$.
nodes.title: Coded machine state

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program with register bound $R$, let $\sigma$ be a register state, and let $n \le R$ and $v$ be natural numbers. The register list of the state obtained from $\sigma$ by setting register $n$ to $v$ equals the register list of $\sigma$ with its entry at position $n$ replaced by $v$.
nodes.title: Updating a register updates the register list

nodes.summary: For a URM program $p$ with register bound $R$, the register list of a register state $\sigma$ is the list $(\sigma(0), \sigma(1), \dots, \sigma(R))$ of the contents of registers $0, \dots, R$.
nodes.title: Register list

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. Suppose there is a URM program that, for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, started with $n$ in register $0$ and all other registers $0$, halts with $f(n)$ in register $0$. Then there is a multi-stack Turing machine that computes $f$ with input and output numbers written in binary: started on the binary word of $n$, it halts with the binary word of $f(n)$.
nodes.title: A URM-computable total function is computed by a multi-stack Turing machine

nodes.summary: Every predicate $P$ on $\mathbb{N}$ that is URM-decidable is decidable by a multi-stack Turing machine.
nodes.title: URM-decidability implies multi-stack decidability

nodes.summary: Every predicate $P$ on $\mathbb{N}$ that is URM-recognizable is recognizable by a multi-stack Turing machine.
nodes.title: URM-recognizability implies multi-stack recognizability

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program with register bound $R$. If an instruction of $p$ writes to register $n$, then $n \le R$.
nodes.title: Written registers lie within the register bound
Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
